title: NCP: Verifier-Guided Optimization of Weight-Space Control Policies
metadata_mismatch: PDF carries subtitle 'Toward Recursive Self-Improvement through Neural Flow Rules' not in metadata title; PDF dated November 5, 2026 vs arXiv v1 9 Nov 2026
why_wsp: A deterministic Python synthesizer (no LLM) proposes temporary, activation-triggered weight interventions (MLP down-projection direction removal, attention head scaling) on SmolLM-135M-Instruct, which a verifier admits or archives into a versioned rule table; weights are restored after every request.
domain: small LM arithmetic QA and token repetition; WikiText-2 perplexity
editor: none (deterministic synthesizer; 'The implemented loop uses a deterministic synthesizer and an explicit verifier')
interface: closed form (projection/scaling templates compiled to W-ISA instruction programs)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (observe, synthesize, verify, admit)
self_editing: no; an external controller applies temporary edits to the served model; framed as a framework for studying RSI at the control-policy level
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: Not given as a count; MLP projection relative spectral change 0.17329298 and head scaling 0.46918526: "The MLP projection had relative spectral change 0.17329298; head scaling had 0.46918526." (Sec 7.3)

headline_results.claim: MLP projection reduced repetition with tiny PPL change
headline_results.quote: One projection reduced validation token repetition from 0.4133 to 0.2191, with a perplexity change of -0.0574%.

headline_results.claim: No candidate improved correctness; none admitted
headline_results.quote: All candidates produced zero newly correct exact answers, so the configured admission gate archived all three and retained the original active policy.
Final exact-answer scoring was 0/3 for both original and routed execution.
Fresh-process repetition and saved-table resumption reproduced the measured outcomes.

cost.quote: The initial end-to-end run took 44.38 seconds. A new-process two-cycle run took 48.37 seconds

baselines_and_controls: Original (empty) active policy vs prospective table on same validation cases; forced-action corpus perplexity vs original weights; parameter-digest restoration checks. No LLM-editor, fine-tune, or random-edit baselines.
runs_and_variance: Single run plus fresh-process repeat and resume (deterministic, greedy decoding); nine-question fixture (3 dev, 3 val, 3 test); no variance reported.
robustness_of_edits: not tested (edits are temporary per-request and restored)
verification: Admission gate: c >= 1 newly correct, r = 0 regressions, Delta repetition >= 0, PPL increase <= 0.5%, exact parameter restoration via SHA-256 digest; optional spectral budget; 25 unit tests. No formal verification.
limitations_stated: Described as an 'architectural microbenchmark' with a nine-question handwritten fixture and 'explicitly bounded corpus slices'; recorded run admitted no rules (active table stayed empty).
code_or_data: none found (MIT license stated; no URL given)
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 Sparks of Weight-Space Programming blog [11]
Aksoy, W-ISA: Transactional Execution of Weight-Space Intervention Programs (companion manuscript) [9]
notes_for_survey: A systems framework (flow-table/control-plane analogy) for proposing, verifying and versioning temporary weight interventions; no LLM proposes edits in the reported run. The only recorded cycle admitted zero rules, so it demonstrates the lifecycle rather than an improvement.
